# A four-embedding sign model for the paired Pell units at 99

Research note, 2026-11-13. Status: manuscript proof with exact arithmetic checks, pending independent review.

The proof below identifies the characteristic-two tetrahedral residual on the four real embeddings of the actual paired-Pell field. A single explicitly given quartic unit has three relative norms whose negative loci give one edge of each perfect matching. This supplies an arithmetic meaning for the edge/complement bit. The value 99 enters through the specified field and unit.

## The four embeddings and the residual

Put \(K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt2,\sqrt{29})\) inside the real numbers, with the displayed square roots positive, and put \(X=\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbb Q}(K,\mathbb R)\). The sign switches of the two square roots form the Klein four group \(G\). They act simply transitively on \(X\), making it an affine plane over \(\mathbb F_2\) with translation group \(G\). Write \(E\subset \mathbb F_2^X\) for the even-weight binary functions on \(X\). These are exactly the affine functions: a nonconstant affine function is 1 at two points, the two constant functions have even weight, and both spaces have dimension three.

Build the complete graph on \(X\). In the mod-two reduction of its integral zero-total endpoint-sum residual, the value at vertex \(v\) is the parity of the sum over the three edges at \(v\). The star-evaluation isomorphism of the [tetrahedral manuscript](https://github.com/awdawmip/enterprise-math/blob/655d6a253e68735e68a59622b4716cb0327da05c/papers/2026-tetrahedral-residuals/YUAN_X_Tetrahedral_Endpoint_Sum_Submission.tex) identifies this residual with \(E\) and its torsion line with the constants. If \(\ell\ne0\) is a linear part, its two possible constant terms give complementary edges. This construction is independent of an ordering of the embeddings.

For a unit \(v\), let \(s_v(x)=1\) exactly when \(x(v)<0\). Signatures add under products. Translation by \(g\in G\) on the input of a signature corresponds to replacing \(v\) by \(g(v)\). For each nonidentity \(g\), the fixed field \(F_g\) is quadratic. Consequently
\[
 s_{N_{K/F_g}v}(x)=s_v(x)+s_v(xg).
\]
In particular, if \(v\) has exactly one negative conjugate, at \(x_0\), then the negative locus of \(N_{K/F_g}v\) is \(\{x_0,x_0g\}\). The three choices of \(g\) give the three edges at \(x_0\), one from each opposite-edge matching. Negating these relative norms gives the three opposite edges.

## One unit, three relative norms

Set \(a=\sqrt2, b=\sqrt{29}\), and let
\[
 \eta=-b+a(13+b)/2.
\]
It is integral, since \((13+b)/2=6+(1+b)/2\) and \((1+b)/2\) is an algebraic integer. Let \(i,j\) switch the signs of \(a,b\), respectively. Direct multiplication gives

| Fixed field | Relative norm of \(\eta\) | Norm to \(\mathbb Q\) |
|---|---|---|
| \(\mathbb Q(b)\) | \(\eta i(\eta)=-70-13b\) | \(-1\) |
| \(\mathbb Q(a)\) | \(\eta j(\eta)=41+29a\) | \(-1\) |
| \(\mathbb Q(ab)\) | \(\eta ij(\eta)=-99+13ab\) | \(-1\) |

Thus \(N_{K/\mathbb Q}\eta=-1\), so \(\eta\) is a unit. At the identity embedding \(\eta>0\), since \((13+b)^2-2b^2=140+26b>0\). The three norm signs there are negative, positive, positive (the last uses \(13^2\cdot58=99^2+1\)). Hence the unique negative embedding of \(\eta\) is \(i\). In order of the table, the negative loci are \(\{1,i\},\{i,ij\},\{i,j\}\).

The positive Pell unit is also recovered from the same relative norm: \((41+29a)(1+a)=99+70a\). It satisfies \(99+70a=(1+a)^6\), and the third relative norm is exactly \((99+13ab)^{-1}\). The remaining quadratic field is tied to the same calculation through \(70+13b=g_{58}^{6}\), using Ramanujan's evaluation \(g_{58}^2=(5+b)/2\). The positive unit \(99+70a\) has empty negative locus: the construction obtains the \(a\)-matching using the negative-norm unit \(41+29a=(1+a)^5\). Here norm sign \(\pm1\) and a conjugate's real sign have different meanings.

## Which signs does the tetrahedron capture?

The signatures of \(-1,1+a,(5+b)/2\) span the constants and the two independent linear characters on \(X\), hence all of \(E\). Conversely, a unit from any quadratic subfield has two repeated pairs of signs on \(X\), so each such signature is even. For an arbitrary unit of the quartic field, having even signature is equivalent to field norm to the rationals \(+1\). It follows that the norm-positive unit signatures are exactly \(E\). Adjoining the odd signature of \(\eta\) gives all sixteen functions on \(X\). Thus the mod-two residual identifies with the signature image of the norm-positive units, with multiplication by \(-1\) realizing its constant-line action.

On these signatures the Galois action is the translation subgroup \(G\) of the full vertex-relabeling group \(S_4\). The constant line still has no \(G\)-invariant additive retraction: for nonzero translation \(g\), choose a linear part with \(\ell(g)=1\). Translation takes an affine lift \(f\) to \(f+1\), contradicting invariance of a retraction which takes the constant 1 to 1. Full \(S_4\) relabels the representation; the four field automorphisms are exactly \(G\). These statements concern the mod-two residual and real signatures. The construction takes the paired-Pell field as input; selecting a distinguished field or recovering the Ramanujan series from an unlabelled graph is a different question.

Dummit and Kisilevsky give the signature matrix for quadratic-subfield units in (14). Their discussion of Kubota's Hilfsatz 3 leading to (15), and their relative-norm formulas in (16), describe how a square root of a product of suitable quadratic units produces signed subfield units. Their Theorem 1 gives signature rank four here: \(2\) and \(29\) satisfy its prime hypotheses, and \(99+13\sqrt{58}\) has quadratic norm \(-1\), so the fundamental unit of \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt{58})\) also has norm \(-1\). [Dummit and Kisilevsky, §4, (14)–(16) and Theorem 1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.04411#page=6).

For the explicit unit above write \(n_g=\eta g(\eta)\) for \(g=i,j,ij\). Multiplying the three relative norms gives
\[
n_i n_j n_{ij}
=\eta^2\!\prod_{g\in G}g(\eta)
=\eta^2N_{K/\mathbb Q}(\eta)
=-\eta^2.
\]
Thus \(\eta^2=-n_i n_j n_{ij}\) realizes the product-square mechanism with the signed Pell units in the table. The vertex star-parity map identifies the negative loci of precisely these three norms with the three edges at \(i\).

## Reproduction

The [exact checker](check_pell_unit_signatures.py) uses rational coefficients in the basis \(1,a,b,ab\), verifies the three relative norms, determines their signs by exact quadratic-field comparisons, and checks all 16 signature patterns and their eight even elements.
